documents.title: Coats technical bulletin: Eliminating Seam Puckering
documents.author: Coats Group
documents.locator: Tension Pucker; Test to identify; Solutions
documents.licenseNotes: Original Stitches paraphrase and direct source link only; no reproduced diagrams or article text.

documents.title: Check a puckered seam on scrap fabric
documents.purpose: Before changing a garment seam, use a short sample made from matching material to test whether thread tension may be contributing to puckering.

documents.title: Thread tension may be contributing
observableSymptoms: Ripples appear along a newly sewn test seam and relax when stitches are removed from a short sample section.
documents.riskNotes: A relaxed sample suggests tension but does not establish the only cause; do not unpick a finished garment from this result alone.

documents.title: Cause remains unresolved
observableSymptoms: A test seam still ripples after a short stitch section is removed, or no controlled sample has been tested.
documents.riskNotes: Other causes include material structure, feeding and needle/thread choice. Do not recommend a particular machine adjustment without another check.

documents.title: Does a test seam relax when the stitches are released?
documents.makerQuestion: On a short, sacrificial seam made from matching scrap fabric, do the ripples flatten when you carefully remove a few centimetres of stitches?
documents.howToCheck: Use scrap material only. Sew a short sample with the same machine, thread and settings. Carefully release both threads along a small section without pulling or damaging the fabric; compare the released and still-stitched sections.
documents.riskNotes: Do not remove stitches from the actual garment for this preliminary test; stop if the sample fabric is being damaged.

documents.title: Compare a lower-tension sample
documents.safeAction: On another scrap seam only, try a modestly lower upper-thread tension while maintaining a balanced stitch. Change one setting at a time and compare it with the original sample.
documents.confirmationCheck: Does the new sample lie flatter while both sides still form a balanced, secure stitch? If not, stop this path and seek another cause.
documents.riskNotes: This is a test-sample experiment, not authorization to alter, unpick or restitch the finished garment.
